power_Standby: Add power_Standby.1hour power_Standby.fast calculates battery life using the delta battery capacity in Ah unit before and after suspend. With platform that have suspend power optimized, the delta can be as low as 0.005 Ah or lower. This makes the rounding error of estimate battery life can be as big as 2-3 days as the battery capacity in Ah unit is reported in 0.001 Ah step. This CL adds 1 hour version to mitigate the problem above. ANDROID: net: ipv6: autoconf routes into per-device tables Currently, IPv6 router discovery always puts routes into RT6_TABLE_MAIN. This causes problems for connection managers that want to support multiple simultaneous network connections and want control over which one is used by default (e.g., wifi and wired). To work around this connection managers typically take the routes they prefer and copy them to static routes with low metrics in the main table. This puts the burden on the connection manager to watch netlink to see if the routes have changed, delete the routes when their lifetime expires, etc. Instead, this patch adds a per-interface sysctl to have the kernel put autoconf routes into different tables. This allows each interface to have its own autoconf table, and choosing the default interface (or using different interfaces at the same time for different types of traffic) can be done using appropriate ip rules. The sysctl behaves as follows: - = 0: default. Put routes into RT6_TABLE_MAIN as before. - > 0: manual. Put routes into the specified table. - < 0: automatic. Add the absolute value of the sysctl to the device's ifindex, and use that table. The automatic mode is most useful in conjunction with net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra_rt_table. A connection manager or distribution could set it to, say, -100 on boot, and thereafter just use IP rules. add clock_gettime to amd64/seccomp When upgrading our VM tests to 4.14, I'm seeing mtpd crash with SIGSYS in __vdso_clock_gettime(). I've seen this in several other daemons too. There are complicated decisions in the kernel VDSO as to whether to use a "fast" user space implementation or to call into the kernel. So this might affect why older kernels didn't see the problem but new ones do. We also might behave differently in a VM vs. real hardware. So, rather than just patch the crash I saw, I tried to guesstimate that anyone using gettimeofday might also want clock_gettime, and that anyone using clock_gettime in an ARM policy might want it in an amd64 policy. crash: Collect BIOS crashes with KernelCollector This patch makes the KernelCollector scan the BIOS log for ARM Trusted Firmware crash signatures (only relevant to ARM64 platforms) and upload them as a kernel crash (with a special signature that clarifies this is a BIOS crash) if found. Even though treating BIOS crashes as "kernel crash" might seem like a bit of a stretch, it makes sense in context: kernel and runtime firmware are deeply intertwined on ARM64 platforms. The kernel calls into ARM Trusted Firmware to do certain operations, and crashes in either may be caused by unexpected behavior in the other. It makes sense to always upload both logs together to give the debugging engineer as much context as possible to understand an issue (especially since BIOS log messages are rare on their own and do not contain timestamps at the moment, making it hard to interpret them in isolation). It therefore makes more sense to treat the KernelCollector as a more general "unexpected reboot from panic in privileged code" collector and share the common infrastructure to process both kinds of logs. Since it doesn't make much sense to handle all completely distinct crash signature types in one GenerateSignature() function, split them out into separate functions again. BUG=chromium:839669 TEST=Added unit test.
